messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency > SLO for /v1/chat/stream on model redwood-v1-int8-calib in us-west-2. Current p99=8.1s (SLO=3s), p95=1.9s (SLO=1s). Traffic spike started ~1768501200. Paging on-call.
Maya: I’m on pager. Investigating. Any deploys or config changes in last 30m?
Alex: I just pushed a quant calibration tweak to redwood-v1-int8-calib canary at 1768501000 — increased aggressive per-layer quant thresholds. Noticed lower token costs in perf tests.
Maya: @Alex can you confirm canary rollout percentage?
Alex: Canary=10% traffic to canary variant, rollout policy was gradual. push id=canary-2026-03-14-02.
perf-bot: perf-check: canary-2026-03-14-02 vs baseline: mean latency -5%, p99 +220% for streaming workloads. Full logs at https://perf.redwood/internal/1745
Kevin: Seeing stream stall traces in tracer: lots of repeated KV cache misses and kernel fallback on a subset of requests — looks correlated to longer sequences and certain token lengths.
Sasha: Are stalls happening only on int8 variant?
Kevin: Yes. fp16 baseline p99 stays ~2.8s. int8-canary p99 spikes to 8s.
Maya: Ok this matches customer reports — we have a live support ticket from AcmePay: multistream sessions experiencing stalls and partial responses. We need immediate mitigation.
Irene: Suggest roll back canary to previous quant profile and remove canary tag. We should also shift traffic off int8 variant for streaming endpoints while we triage.
Daniel: I can push a routing rule to redirect /v1/chat/stream to redwood-v1-fp16-fallback for 100% of traffic in us-west-2 for 15m. Do we want to do that?
Maya: Yes. Do it. Also start a rollback for the calibration change.
Patrick: On it — issuing commands now.
deploy-bot: Command accepted: redwood-cli route set --path /v1/chat/stream --model redwood-v1-fp16-fallback --region us-west-2 --duration 15m --author Patrick
deploy-bot: Command accepted: redwood-cli rollout undo --model redwood-v1-int8-calib --to-tag stable --author Patrick
Alex: Rolling back canary config (removing canary routing and restoring stable quant profile). Watch for requeueing.
Maya: Can someone confirm whether Dedicated and Private customers are affected?
Irene: Private deployments unaffected. Dedicated pools: one enterprise cluster (Edulogic-prod) had a small percent of traffic routed to the canary yesterday via experimentation pipeline — reaching out to SE.
Alex: Confirmed — Edulogic had canary=5%. Notified their SE.
perf-bot: Metric update: 1768501400 p99=6.9s, 1768501500 p99=4.5s, 1768501600 p99=3.1s in us-west-2 after routing change.
Kevin: Traces show that the quant calibration caused some weight scales to produce out-of-range activations triggering slower fallback path in the custom kernel (non-quant path) for certain attention patterns -> tail explosion. The calibration reduced variance on some layers but created edge-case numeric blowups.
Maya: Good quick diagnostic. Action items: (1) keep fp16 routing for streaming for 30m, (2) fully revert int8-canary, (3) surface incident to customers impacted, (4) run targeted regression tests that simulate long streaming sessions and repetitive prefixes.
Daniel: Routing now extended 30m. deploy-bot: Command accepted: redwood-cli route update --path /v1/chat/stream --duration 30m --author Daniel
Patrick: Revert confirmed, canary removed, int8 variant marked quarantined. deploy-bot: rollout status undo -> success.
Alex: I’m attaching the exact calibration diff: ```diff --git a/quant_profiles/v1.calib b/quant_profiles/v1.calib
index 7f3..c9a 100644
--- a/quant_profiles/v1.calib
+++ b/quant_profiles/v1.calib
@@ -12,7 +12,7 @@
- layer_norm_threshold = 0.025
+ layer_norm_threshold = 0.010  # aggressive tweak
 per_channel = true
 fallback_policy = "kernel_fallback"
 calibrate_attention = true
```
Maya: That threshold drop looks suspicious. Might have amplified round-off on a subset of long-context attention.
Irene: Customer comms draft: "We observed elevated latency and streaming stalls for chat streaming endpoints in us-west-2 due to an int8 calibration change; we have routed streaming traffic to the fp16 fallback and reverted the calibration. We are investigating root cause and will follow up." Approve?
Maya: Approve. Send to AcmePay + Edulogic and post status update to status.redwood.com.
Patrick: Sending now. Notifying account reps.
perf-bot: Post-mitigation metrics: 1768502200 p95=0.9s, p99=2.6s (us-west-2). Baseline p99 target 3.0s.
Kevin: We should also add synthetic streaming checks that vary token lengths and force KV cache misses — the current canary perf run didn't exercise the long-tail.
Alex: Agree. Will add extended synthetic canary workload and a streaming-specific HWM (high-water mark) alert for p99 > 2x baseline.
Maya: On-call handoff in 30m to @Sasha. Sasha, recap: canary reverted, streaming traffic routed to fp16 fallback for 30m extended, quarantined int8 calibration, customers notified, metrics trending back under SLO. Please continue watching logs and traces for any residual stalls.
Sasha: Got it. I’ll take over and keep monitoring until stable.
Irene: Postmortem owners? Alex + Kevin to own root cause and fix new quant calibration validation. Maya to own customer comms and runbook update.
Alex: Will add stricter regression tests and a canary gating check for streaming stalls; plan to add an automated rollback on p99 regression for canary > 5% traffic.
Daniel: Also recommend adding a temporary guard in the planner to avoid routing long streaming sessions to aggressive int8 variants until we have more confidence.
Maya: Thanks team. Recording: incident-severity=sev2, impact=partial degradation for streaming endpoints in us-west-2, duration ~45m to mitigation. Follow-up: postmortem with timeline, calibration diffs, synthetic test add, new canary gating rules.
Sasha: Acknowledged, taking on-call. I’ll update this thread if anything new shows up.
incident-bot: Incident update recorded. Incident ID: INC-2026-03-14-002. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-03-14-002
Patrick: closing loop with AcmePay SE — their sessions back to normal. They reported occasional lag around 1768501300-1768501700 but no data loss.
Maya: Great. When stable for 1h we can restore normal routing and unquarantine the int8 variant for further testing behind stricter canary gates.
Sasha: Will monitor for 1h, then coordinate with Alex for next safe canary.
Daniel: Adding follow-up task tickets now.
Maya: Thanks everyone, nice work on the fast rollback and routing change.
